gallery.description: Photo by R. W. Rynerson, Winter 1969-70 shows Armored Personnel Carrier and Jeep of the 4th Battalion, 18th Infantry Regiment of the U.S. Army's Berlin Brigade passing through a Berlin-Zehlendorf residential street intersection under the eyes of a soldier from Headquarters Company of that unit.  Alerts occurred monthly as a training exercise, but occasionally additional alerts signalled the receipt of intelligence information on Warsaw Pact maneuvers around the isolated city.

gallery.description: A significant part of the Berlin Brigade's duty involved patrolling the border, especially the Berlin Wall. These patrols were a visible sign of the US military's presence and commitment to defending West Berlin. The b/w photo was colored AI.

gallery.title: File:1979-04-29 Berlin-Reinickendorf Flughafen Berlin-Tegel (West-Berlin) a.jpg
gallery.description: The departure boards show some of the destinations from Berlin-Tegel Airport. At that time, destinations in West Germany accounted for the majority of the flight schedule. There were also charter flights to the rest of the world.

gallery.title: File:1987-01-11 West-Berlin Berlin-Schöneberg Südgelände a.jpg
gallery.description: In 1879, the Tempelhof repair shop was built on the southern site, followed ten years later by the Tempelhof marshalling yard. From 1923 to 1931, it was expanded into a high-performance marshalling yard for the Halle/Leipzig-Berlin and Dresden-Berlin rail lines. The 50-meter-high water tower was built there in 1927, and the Priesterweg station was built in 1928. In 1952, marshalling operations ceased, and the western operational area of ​​Tempelhof was abandoned. With the construction of the Berlin Wall, the site lost all of its importance.
categories: January 1987 in rail transport in West Berlin

gallery.title: File:1987-01-11 West-Berlin Berlin-Schöneberg Südgelände Prellerweg b.jpg
gallery.description: In the background, the rubble mountain "Insulaner". The name was chosen through an ideas competition in which 180 Schöneberg school classes participated. The name suggestion was based on the then-popular cabaret "Die Insulaner" (The Insulaner) on the radio station RIAS. On August 11, 1951, the Insulaner was officially named.

gallery.title: File:1987-01-11 Berlin-Charlottenburg Kantstraße Fasanenstraße Kantdreieck a.jpg
gallery.description: The Kant Triangle between Kantstraße, Fasanenstraße, and the railway line has been as it has been for decades. But it won’t stay that way.

gallery.title: File:1987-05-08 West-Berlin Berlin-Charlottenburg Kantstraße Fasanenstraße a.jpg
gallery.description: The Kant triangle between Kantstraße, Fasanenstraße, and the railway line is showing its transformation. The Esso gas station and the Guse K.G. car rental company have been demolished.

gallery.filename: 1983 West-Berlin Bezirk Berlin-Tempelhof OT Lichtenrade S-Bahnhof h.jpg
gallery.title: File:1983 West-Berlin Bezirk Berlin-Tempelhof OT Lichtenrade S-Bahnhof h.jpg
gallery.description: Pictured here is an S-Bahn train of the German Reichsbahn of the GDR on the N I line with the circulation number 5. The line to Frohnau was served every 20 minutes with a half-train, i.e. with only four carriages, and led through the north-south tunnel under East Berlin, stopping only once at Friedrichstraße station.

gallery.filename: 1989-05-01 West-Berlin Berlin-Zehlendorf Havel Sacrow Grenztonne Nr.13 (DDR) b.jpg
gallery.title: File:1989-05-01 West-Berlin Berlin-Zehlendorf Havel Sacrow Grenztonne Nr.13 (DDR) b.jpg
gallery.description: GDR border buoy No. 13. These buoys marked the water border between the GDR and West Berlin. The buoys were spaced between 100 and 200 meters apart, depending on geographical necessity.

gallery.title: File:1989-08-13 West-Berlin Charlottenburg Bonhoefferufer.jpg
gallery.description: Currently (2026), construction work is underway at this site to restore the embankment stabilization. The objective is to reinstate a promenade, including vegetation.

gallery.title: File:1986-06-22 West-Berlin Charlottenburg Westend Olympiastadion b.jpg
gallery.description: On a Sunday without an event, you are almost entirely alone in the stadium. And that is precisely how this monumental structure strikes and impresses you.

gallery.title: File:1986-06-22 West-Berlin Charlottenburg Westend Olypiastadion a.jpg
gallery.description: The Olympic Gate forms part of the main entrance on the eastern side of the stadium. The North Tower (on the left in the image) is named the Preussen Tower, while the South Tower (on the right in the image) is named the Bayern Tower. Situated to the east, in front of it, lies the Olympic Square, facing towards Westend.

gallery.title: File:1987-09-27 West-Berlin Schmargendorf Hohenzollerndamm.jpg
gallery.description: The Hohenzollerdamm Bridge spans the urban motorway and the railway tracks. Visible on the left are the station building and the entrance to the Hohenzollerndamm S-Bahn station. On the right, the curved building at Seesener Straße 1 was erected in the 1930s as the administrative headquarters of the "Berliner Städtische Wasserwerke AG" (Berlin Municipal Waterworks). Behind it stands the gleaming silver office tower of the Federal Insurance Institute for Salaried Employees (BfA).

gallery.title: File:1989-03-12 West-Berlin Steglitz S-Bahnhof.jpg
gallery.description: West Berlin’s BVG had resumed operations on the Wannsee Line in February 1985. The railway bridges passing over Albrechtstraße also created a bottleneck for road traffic, as they were too low. They were raised in succession, first the S-Bahn tracks (including the platform) and subsequently the freight tracks. All work was completed by May 1992.

gallery.title: File:1986-12-23 West-Berlin Charlottenburg S-Bahnhof Westkreuz.jpg
gallery.description: After the BVG was granted operating rights for the S-Bahn in West Berlin in 1984, the rolling stock was refurbished alongside the renovation of the tracks. In some of the carriages, the wooden benches were replaced with individual upholstered seats.

gallery.title: File:1982-11-XX West-Berlin Tempelhof Mariendorf S-Bahnhof.jpg
gallery.description: Advertising related to the GDR was frequently found on railway premises in West Berlin, given that the GDR’s Deutsche Reichsbahn held both the operating rights and the obligation to operate there. At the platform above, a train from the NI service group is shown arriving from Frohnau, bound for Lichtenrade.

gallery.title: File:1983-12-30 West-Berlin Reinickendorf Eichborndamm.jpg
gallery.description: The station was located on the Deutsche Reichsbahn (GDR) S-Bahn line NII, running from Lichterfelde Süd to Heiligensee. Half-trains of the Class 275 (ET 165) series operated at 20-minute intervals. The line was closed after the BVG took over S-Bahn operations in West Berlin. It reopened in May 1995 as line S25, with the station now named Eichborndamm.

gallery.title: File:1983-09-XX West-Berlin Reinickendorf S-Bahnhof Schönholz.jpg
gallery.description: Train group NI (running between Frohnau and Lichtenrade) and train group NII (running between Heiligensee and Lichterfelde Süd) stopped here. The last Deutsche Reichsbahn trains called at Schönholz on January 8, 1984. The following day, the Reichsbahn suspended operations on this line, as the operating rights were henceforth held by the West Berlin BVG.
